messages.author: Michael Shokhen
messages.body:
Dear AMBER experts,
The periodic water box is corrupted by minimization procedure.
See scripts and figures below.
I need your advice how to resolve the problem.
Thank you,
Michael
The initial system (protein in water box) was generated by
the tleap.in script:
source leaprc.protein.ff14SB
source leaprc.water.tip3p
mc = loadpdb  protein_nh.pdb
solvateBox mc TIP3PBOX 16
addIonsRand mc Na+ 296 Cl- 308
saveAmberParm mc mc.prmtop mc.inpcrd
quit
The next step was the water minimization only,
restraining the protein by min1.in script:
Minimize water
System minimization:
&cntrl
imin=1, ntmin=1, nmropt=0, drms=0.1
maxcyc=20000, ncyc=1500,
ntx=1, irest=0,
ntpr=100, ntwr=100, iwrap=0,
ntf=1, ntb=1, cut=8.0, nsnb=20,
igb=0,
ibelly=0, ntr=1,
restraintmask="!:WAT", restraint_wt=10.0,
&end
/
[cid:d0b8a807-cb5f-46b3-a980-2d3e2ae46f6b]
*****************************
Michael Shokhen, PhD
Associate Professor
Department of Chemistry
Bar Ilan University,
Ramat Gan, 52900
Israel

messages.author: Nagar, Hemant
messages.body:
Hi,
Try with this .trajin script to extract out your frames.
trajin prod_run.nc                 " (.nc file from production run)"
autoimage
center :a -b mass origin         "[a(first residue number)-b(last residue number), # residue number in your file]"
image origin center
trajout prod_run_frames_COM.pdb ( output file name)
Regards,
Hemant

messages.author: Michael Shokhen
messages.body:
Dear Prof. Case,
Thank you for your response on my report
about the corrupted periodic water box.
You addressed me to the analogous error report from October 6-th
where Prof. Cheatham suggested that it is �likely just an artifact of
the visualization.�
I have identified that the error source is the command �autoimage origin�
in the cpptr_pdb.in file:
parm ../mc.prmtop
trajin mdcrd 700000 700000
autoimage origin
cpptraj_pdb.in
trajout heat.pdb pdb
run
quit
The autoimage origin command must be deleted there.
See the attached figure for illustration.
Michael

messages.author: Daniel Roe
messages.body:
Hi,
On Sat, Nov 6, 2021 at 12:19 PM Michael Shokhen
<michael.shokhen.biu.
ac.il> wrote:
> I have identified that the error source is the command “autoimage origin”
This isn't an error. You've simply imaged the system in a different
way. With periodic boundary conditions, both pictures are equivalent.
The 'autoimage' command by default will try to center the picture on
the first molecule. Based on the results from 'autoimage', it seems
like you may need more of a buffer in your system (unless for some
reason you need that particular concentration).
-Dan
